teams.heading: Fiji concede 145 points over three opening Nations Championship losses
teams.body: Fiji have conceded 145 points in their opening three Nations Championship fixtures. They have scored 49 points across those same three matches. This leaves the side with a points difference of minus 96. Their latest result was a 17-33 defeat against Scotland. Fiji are aiming to rebuild towards their highest-ever world ranking of No. 7, which they achieved in 2023. Their next test is against France.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick faces scrutiny over squad progress under landmark £264m deal
teams.body: With the 2027 World Cup now only 12 months away, scrutiny has intensified over whether Steve Borthwick’s side is reaping the rewards of the Rugby Football Union’s £264 million investment. The landmark professional game partnership allows Borthwick to award 25 enhanced contracts, providing him with unprecedented control over the conditioning and development of his elite players within the Premiership. While the domestic league continues to thrive under the new financial structure, the national side remains under pressure to convert this strategic autonomy into world-leading results.

teams.heading: France sustain momentum as they secure two straight test wins
teams.body: France head into the final international block of the year on a solid footing, having secured victories in three of their last five matches. The team is currently enjoying a run of two straight wins, most recently producing a convincing 42-15 result against Japan in the July Nations Championship group stage. With three matches played in the tournament so far, Les Bleus will look to build on this recent form when they return to action in November.

teams.heading: Ireland women make six changes for Sunday fixture against Japan
teams.body: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has reshuffled his side following last weekend's 40-36 defeat by the USA. Béibhinn Parsons, Anna McGann, and Aoibheann Reilly return to the backline, while Eilís Cahill earns her first start in the front row alongside Neve Jones. In the back row, Brittany Hogan is recalled to the starting lineup. Crucially, Aoife Wafer has been ruled out of the contest after sustaining a minor injury in training earlier this week.

teams.heading: Zebre Parma Falls To Seven-Try Bulls In Opening URC Defeat
teams.body: Zebre suffered a heavy 47-13 defeat against the Bulls in their United Rugby Championship opener in Parma on Saturday. Despite an early penalty goal from Tommaso Allan, the hosts struggled to maintain momentum after Matteo Canali was sent to the sin-bin. Captain Alessandro Fusco provided a moment of individual brilliance in the final quarter, stepping through the defence to score, but the visitors proved too clinical, crossing for seven tries to secure a dominant victory on the road.

teams.heading: Glasgow bench inspires dramatic second-half comeback victory against Munster
teams.body: Glasgow Warriors secured a 26-20 victory over Munster at Thomond Park in Saturday's opening round of the United Rugby Championship. Despite trailing by 10 points at the interval, the visitors clawed their way back through a second-half resurgence. The introduction of the Scottish bench proved decisive, providing the necessary impact to dismantle the Munster defence. Tries from Nathan McBeth, George Horne, and a late score from Horne himself ensured the Warriors departed Limerick with a hard-fought bonus-point win.

teams.heading: Wales women suffer narrow defeat against USA in Cardiff contest
teams.body: Wales women fell to a 26-24 defeat against a clinical USA side at Cardiff Arms Park on Saturday. Despite scoring tries through Keira Bevan, Kelsey Jones, Sisilia Tuipulotu and Alex Callender, the hosts were undone by an error-strewn performance and a hat-trick from Eagles number eight Freda Tafuna. Head coach Sean Lynn remained positive regarding his side's resilience, noting: "I saw some grit, I saw some effort there," as the team now turns its attention to next month’s fixtures against Japan.

teams.heading: Men sentenced for murder of former Argentina international Federico Aramburu
teams.body: A French court has sentenced two men to lengthy prison terms for the 2022 murder of former Argentina international Federico Aramburu in Paris. Loik Le Priol received a 26-year sentence, with the court noting his intent to kill, while associate Romain Bouvier was sentenced to 19 years for attempted murder. Aramburu, who earned 22 caps for Los Pumas, was killed following an altercation near the Boulevard Saint-Germain. The defendants have 10 days to appeal the court's ruling.

teams.heading: Australia women defeat Scotland with dominant second-half performance
teams.body: The Australia women’s side secured a 30-10 victory over Scotland in Edinburgh, overcoming a 10-5 half-time deficit. Following a clinical first half from the hosts, the Wallaroos seized control with three tries in an eight-minute spell after the interval. Scrum-half Samantha Wood, who converted her own try to initiate the turnaround, alongside scorers Desiree Miller, Brianna Hoy and Faitala Moleko, ensured a comfortable win for the visitors. The two sides are scheduled to meet again in Sydney next weekend.

teams.body: The Sakura XV face Ireland in Galway today, looking to reset after recent international outings. Ireland, currently ranked 5th, are targeting a strong response following their loss to the USA. Japan will need to manage the hosts' early momentum, as Ireland have proven particularly potent in opening halves.

teams.heading: New Zealand women lose to England following late Zoe Harrison try
teams.body: The Black Ferns saw their eight-match winning streak under coach Whitney Hansen ended by England in a 26-19 defeat at Twickenham. Despite holding a half-time lead following tries from Amy Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga, New Zealand were eventually undone by a last-gasp interception try from Zoe Harrison. The result marks New Zealand's fourth consecutive loss to the Red Roses, though captain Georgia Ponsonby noted the side’s resilient performance throughout the barnstorming contest.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus explains Marco van Staden selection at number eight
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has clarified the tactical thinking behind starting Marco van Staden at number eight for the upcoming clash against the Wallabies. The coach noted that the position requires one specific technical prerequisite: “you only scrum at number eight.” While some observers have questioned the selection given other available options, Erasmus emphasised that the loose trio remains balanced by the inclusion of taller options like Elrigh Louw and specialist breakdown threats, ensuring the Springboks maintain their physical identity at the set-piece.
